title: आधुनिक नेपाली उपन्यासको नवीन चरण {New Phase of Modern Nepali Novel}

american_english: For the systematic study of the modern Nepali novel, it has been studied by dividing it into different phases. In those periodizations, novels after the year 2036 B.S. have been discussed by placing them into a single phase as contemporary trends. However, the study of later-period novels confirms that the use of postmodernist tendencies differing from tradition has begun to occur extensively in recent Nepali novels. Because postmodernism is a collective term for diverse tendencies, novels of diverse tendencies have been created in substantial numbers within its broad scope. A definitive time-indicative word such as contemporaneity cannot encompass them. Furthermore, contemporaneity is not a theory-based tendency either. Therefore, identifying its distinct tendencies and pinpointing their starting point through comprehensive study and analysis of recent Nepali novels is a desirable undertaking for Nepali novel criticism. For this purpose, the present research has been conducted focusing on resolving the problem of what kind of new tendencies have appeared in later Nepali novels and how modern Nepali novels can be divided into phases on their basis. In this process, the problem presented above has been resolved based on previous studies conducted regarding the periodization of modern Nepali novels and regarding later novels, as well as on reading and analyzing novels characterized by new tendencies. From the research conducted in this manner, it confirms that a thoroughly postmodernist phase began in Nepali fiction starting from Dhruba Chandra Gautam and Dhruba Sapkota's novel "Jyaga," and because sufficient novels endowed with diverse postmodernist tendencies were subsequently published both qualitatively and quantitatively, it is concluded that a new phase began in the modern Nepali novel after 2050 B.S.
